The Study Reader

The e-reader way — the verses open in front of you, each with its full analysis.

  • Complete word-by-word breakdown of every verse
  • अन्वयः, कारकचक्रम् and पदपरिचयः for every verse, in Sanskrit
  • Transliteration you can show or hide
  • Best for: close study, revision, reference

Option B — The Study Reader

Modelled on the Samsaadhanii e-reader: choose a verse and study it whole — text, transliteration, translation, word-by-word table, and now also the अन्वयः, the कारकचक्रम् and a पदपरिचयः table naming each word's form — नामपदम्, क्रियापदम् or अव्ययपदम् — with its लिङ्ग-विभक्ति-वचन or लकार-पुरुष-वचन.

The Guided Path

A Duolingo-style trail through the chapter — one verse per stop, a few minutes each.

  • Tap any word — पदपरिचयः says whether it is a नामपदम् or a क्रियापदम्
  • Every verse carries its अन्वयः and a कारकचक्रम्, as in the Samsaadhanii e-reader
  • Almost everything in Sanskrit — English kept to a minimum
  • Best for: a daily habit, beginners

Verse text: Śrīmad Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 1, verses 1–47, Chapter 2, verses 1–72, Chapter 3, verses 1–43, Chapter 4, verses 1–42, Chapter 5, verses 1–29, Chapter 6, verses 1–47, Chapter 7, verses 1–30, Chapter 8, verses 1–28, Chapter 9, verses 1–34, Chapter 10, verses 1–42, Chapter 11, verses 1–55, Chapter 12, verses 1–20, and Chapter 13, verses 1–34 — as presented in the Samsaadhanii e-reader (Computational Linguistics Group, University of Hyderabad). The अन्वयः word order, कारकचक्रम् relations and पदपरिचयः tables here are the e-reader's own analysis, reproduced exactly as its data gives them — nothing re-tagged, reordered or corrected; words the analysis supplies but the verse omits are shown in brackets, and the speaker lines are marked as not part of that analysis. A word the analysis lists more than once keeps a row for each occurrence. Translations and word glosses are short learner renderings.
